name: Keiichiro Nakamura
event: UFC Fight Night: Bonfim vs. Brady
summary: A Japanese featherweight (8-1, age 28; EXFIGHT) and the Road to UFC Season 4 featherweight tournament winner. Seven of his eight wins are KO/TKOs, and he has won eight straight since losing his pro debut. He came from two rounds down to stop Sebastian Szalay with a knee in R3 of the final.

how_they_fight.Striking: Power striker who uses knees as a finisher. Knee up the middle on Eoh Jin Park's takedown attempt in R2 of the quarterfinal; knee to the chin to drop Szalay in R3 (Cageside Press). Works from range with front kicks early, then turns to pressure. Five straight R1 KO/TKOs on the Japanese regional scene before Road to UFC.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Defensive. Park went 0 for 6 on takedowns against him. Szalay got a takedown in R2 of the final. His only loss was an R3 submission in his 2022 pro debut.
how_they_fight.Defense: Was out-struck 79-45 by Szalay and hurt by a head clash in R2; Cageside described him as wild and off-balance in that round. He absorbs about 4.4 significant strikes per minute.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: A slow starter in his best tests, then dangerous late. Against Szalay he was down two rounds on all cards before the R3 finish; Park went into R2; his semifinal with Kaiwen Li went 15 minutes. Against regional opposition his finishes came in R1. Showed he can raise his pace in R3 when behind.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Composed when behind. UFC.com describes him as a confident heel who smirks at partisan crowds. Coming off a nine-month layoff since the final.

patterns: Seven KO/TKO wins; knees are his signature finisher
Slow start against good opposition, strong R3 (came from two rounds down to stop Szalay)
concerns: Gave away rounds against Szalay and was out-struck
Can look wild and off-balance under pressure
keys_to_beat: Win R1-R2 with volume and pressure, but don't change levels carelessly into his knees
Wrestle him; he's rarely been put on his back
Expect him to come forward in R3

news.text: Won the Road to UFC Season 4 featherweight final with an R3 TKO (knee, then punches) of Sebastian Szalay at UFC 325.
Beat Kaiwen Li by unanimous decision (29-27, 29-28, 29-28) in the semifinal.
